shots.line: Three ways people can tell your product video is AI.
One, the letters on the label melt.
shots.room: kitchen counter with skincare bottles bright

shots.line: Two, the hand grabs the product with too many fingers. Three, the product changes size between shots.
shots.room: home office desk monitor editing bright

shots.line: The kit has a seven point check that catches all three, and the free fix for each. DM me kit.

twin.title: Your AI video in your own voice

shots.line: Your AI video doesn't have to sound like a stranger.
Make the clip with an AI video tool first, so the lips move on their own.
Then run the audio through a voice changer with your own cloned voice. The timing stays the same, so the lips still match.
That's how I make these without filming. Follow for more AI video tips.

lines.say: If you post the same clip with a new voiceover, TikTok can treat it as unoriginal.
Make each video a different shape instead.
Result first. Side by side. Three things. In the moment. Unbox to use. Gift reveal.
Each one comes with its own shot list in the AI Product Video Kit.
Three fixes for AI talking videos.
One. Write keywords in lowercase. When I wrote kit in capitals, the AI spelled it out letter by letter.
Two. Don't ask it to count on fingers. Mine went thumb, middle finger, then index.
Three. Give every shot its own camera angle and room. It looks like a real shoot.
Save this for your next video.
